review.finding: Prose claims no unit row carries a `worktree` field pre-R5a ("Pre-R5a no row carries a worktree field yet"), but R2 (#784) already writes it: unit_lease.py:187-194 sets `"worktree": str(worktree)` and sub-iterate-runner.md:36-39 calls check_unit_lease.py touch before Step 4/5. The fallback at L252-255 is dead code on the normal path today, and R5a's author is told (L285-288) to rely on a branch that isn't taken. Not a live bug (both sides read the same field), but a false load-bearing claim in a guaranteed-loaded runtime prompt.
review.suggestion: Reword to: the row normally carries `worktree` (written by unit_lease.touch at each runner step boundary); the fallback covers a row touched before R2's lease landed or a lease touch that failed (warn-and-continue).

review.finding: The round's headline fix -- scoping the diff itself (diff_head/$diff) to $unit_wt instead of {project_root} -- has no test guarding it. Existing assertions (`"merge-base" in step`, `"diff_head=$(git" in step`) are satisfied verbatim by `git -C "{project_root}"` too; reverting campaign-mode.md:294-295 back to {project_root} leaves every test in the file green. Given this sub-iterate was REJECTed twice already for exactly this class of silent {project_root} call site, the diff needs its own mutation-probed guard.
review.suggestion: Add assertions anchored on the unit-scoped forms, e.g. `'diff_head=$(git -c "$unit_wt" rev-parse head)' in step` and `'git -c "$unit_wt" diff' in step` (note: harness lowercases -C to -c, see LOW 6 below).

review.finding: $unit_wt is resolved at L252 and consumed at L256/294-295/353/357/364, but the `fires` decision at L296-297 is a model judgement made from the diff body that in practice forces a fresh Bash call before pin runs at L335. campaign-mode.md's own L239-242 states a fresh Bash call starts with an empty environment. In that fresh call $unit_wt is empty, and the NEW equality check at L353 ([ "$pin_wt" = "$unit_wt" ]) turns that loss into a STRICT-STOP on the happy path -- a new failure mode this commit introduced (prior post-pin checks used literal {project_root} or same-call values). $fires being lost in the same window also silently appends --review-skipped to a pin for a unit that IS being reviewed. Fails closed but halts a healthy campaign.
review.suggestion: Either state explicitly that L252-364 must run as ONE Bash call, or dual-write $unit_wt/$diff_head/$fires to $run_dir/ before the fires judgement and re-read them at the top of the pin block, matching the pattern already used at L394/L417 for run_dir/pr_url/unit_wt across the a/b/c spawn boundary.

review.finding: If the inner `git -C "$unit_wt" merge-base origin/{default} "$diff_head"` fails, the substitution collapses and git sees `...{sha}` (HEAD...{sha}), an empty diff for diff_head==HEAD. Empty diff -> fires=0 -> cascade skipped -> unit merges unreviewed. Fail-open. Pre-dates this commit structurally but the line was rewritten here.
review.suggestion: Capture `base=$(git -C "$unit_wt" merge-base ...) || STRICT-STOP` before building the diff command.

review.finding: The jq lookup is not identical to resolve_unit_identity() (review_attribution.py:92-103): jq case-folds with ascii_downcase (ASCII only) vs Python's exact-match-first then .lower() (Unicode). A row with .id null/non-string aborts the WHOLE jq program (poisoning every unit's resolution); two rows differing only in case emit two lines, making $unit_wt multi-line and cd fail. Currently fail-closed via the new pin_wt check, but the failure mode is confusing.
review.suggestion: Use `select((.id? // "") | ascii_downcase == ...)` with first-match semantics, or drop the claim that the two lookups are identical.

review.finding: 2>/dev/null on the jq call conflates jq-missing, malformed loop_state.json, and genuinely-no-worktree-field into the same {project_root} fallback, producing a STRICT-STOP message pointing at the wrong root cause downstream.
review.suggestion: Capture jq's exit status (`unit_wt=$(jq ...) || STRICT-STOP`) or let stderr through.

review.finding: `unit_wt=$(cat "$run_dir/unit_worktree" 2>/dev/null || echo "{project_root}")` does not fall back on an EMPTY file -- cat succeeds, $unit_wt is "", cd "" returns 0 without moving, gh pr view silently runs in the campaign worktree. Post-R5a this is the exact misattribution class R3 exists to close. The write producing this file (L357) is the only unguarded state-write in the step.
review.suggestion: Apply the same `[ -n "$unit_wt" ] || unit_wt="{project_root}"` idiom this commit introduced at L255, and guard the echo with `|| STRICT-STOP`. Same empty-value exposure exists at the bare cats around L394, L417, L480.

review.finding: The reordered post-cascade `pr_url=$(cd "$unit_wt" && gh pr view ...)` is unchecked, contradicting the adjacent prose claim at L419 that "every command is CHECKED". Its pre-pin sibling (L256-258) does guard with `[ -n "$pr_url" ] && [ "$pr_url" != "null" ] || STRICT-STOP`.
review.suggestion: Mirror the pre-pin guard on the post-cascade pr_url.

review.finding: The prose harness lowercases text, so assertions read `git -c "$unit_wt"` and `headrefname,baserefname` -- a reader has no way to know `-c` is a normalized `-C` (a real, different git flag) without knowing the harness internals.
review.suggestion: Add a module-level comment explaining the lowercase normalization, or a norm()-applying helper for expected strings.

review.finding: Test named `..._run_dir_and_gh_pr_view_are_unit_scoped_...` asserts the OPPOSITE for run_dir (stays {project_root}), with a stale justification ("circular dependency on the very value it exists to produce") that this same commit's own ADR bullet refutes for the diff -- $unit_wt is now provably resolvable before anything else runs. The real reason run_dir stays at {project_root} is that the runner writes DONE/result.json there and pin roots runs/ there via --project-root.
review.suggestion: Replace the stale rationale in the test docstring/comment with the real one, to avoid a future reviewer bouncing on the same disproven argument.

review.suggestion: Update the heading to reflect current state or make it clear it's historical (first crossing) and point to the latest entry.
